title: Active nematic colony SIMD replicates on seed 3: 25 persistent splits, generation 4, 53 tracks >= 1 BL; zeta=0 gives 6 static round droplets
summary: Fresh seed 3, t=1000. From white noise, faint nuclei appear by t=40; two acquire order and become rods with a vortex pair by t=85, elongate, pinch and split, and their descendants spread until ~31 rods fill the domain by t~800 (rerun/sheet.png). labkit: 46 splits, 25 persistent, max generation 4, merge/split 0.24; 53 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length (max 3.4 BL, 0.09/time). Passive twin zeta=0 on the same seed: 6 round droplets, 0 splits, max 0.7 BL.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: white noise over the whole domain
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png and rerun/tracks.png: discrete rods of similar length, 31 at t=1000
observations.M: rerun/FACTS.md: 53 tracks >= 1 BL, max 3.4 BL; zeta0/ max 0.7 BL
observations.D: rerun/lineage.png and FACTS.md: 25 persistent splits, generation 4; rods pinch at the centre in rerun/sheet.png t=135-305

verdicts.limitation: Motion is short (max 3.4 BL in t=1000) and partly jostling in a crowded colony; 3 BL counts for M but the swimming is weak. The rods' material comes from the chemostat term (an open supply), so growth is imposed by the bath. No resolution check by me; the author reports faster motion at dt/2, so motility speed is not converged.
